sources_opened.pages: printed pp. 53-54 (PDF pp. 61-62: Theorem 2.1.21 and the following remarks, definition of nice, Theorem 2.1.22, caveat and cardinality remark) and app. A.3 pp. 464-466 (PDF pp. 472-474: Theorem A.3.1, Example A.3.2, proof, Lemma A.3.3); pp. 53-54 also viewed as rendered page images; held per spec/coverage/edition-2026/held-sources.json

components.note: Real sequences, coordinates, first-n projections, Borel cylinders, the half-open rectangle semialgebra with -inf <= a < b <= inf (Durrett app. A.3, p. 464) and F_infinity = sigma(S) are all stated. The p. 53 generating family {omega: omega_i in B_i, i <= n} lies between S and the Borel-cylinder algebra C, and lines 62-66 prove sigma(A) = sigma(C) = F_infinity, so the source's two product sigma-field definitions coincide on the route.
Consistency on rectangles exactly as in Theorems 2.1.21 and A.3.1 (allowing infinite endpoints); the bounded-endpoint sufficiency claim is proved by pi-system uniqueness.

Semialgebra, both algebras, sigma-field equality, consistency on all Borel bases, well-definedness, finite additivity, mass one, monotonicity and finite subadditivity all proved with written steps; corresponds to the finite-union case of the A.3 proof (p. 465).
Open-cover compactness and tightness of finite-dimensional probabilities defined.

Compactness of closed bounded rectangles (bisection plus countable-basis reduction), unions, closed subsets, tightness, and the inner approximation by finite unions of closed rectangles used in Lemma A.3.3 (p. 465), all with written proofs.

Lemma A.3.3 (pp. 465-466): the delta/2^(n+1) approximation, D_n, compactness of D_n*, the nested diagonal subsequence and the contradiction are all written; the source's 'repeat sets' device is replaced by an explicitly stated strictly increasing prefix dimension.
Theorem 2.1.21 / A.3.1 with existence, uniqueness and the decomposition P(A) = sum P(A_i) + P(B_n) of the A.3 proof; extension via the routed premeasure theorem thm:p15-premeasure-extension.
Independent sequences with prescribed laws, including Example A.3.2 with distribution functions F_i (annex lines 256-264), the decreasing-product formula and the dyadic identification, all proved.

components.gap: ED26-P15-CH-countable-product-measures-C009 (partial): Durrett PTE v5 (2019-01-11), p. 53, defines (S,S) to be nice when there is a one-to-one map phi from S into R with phi and phi^{-1} both measurable (no clause requiring phi(S) to be Borel), remarks that such spaces are often called standard Borel spaces, and says the next result shows that most spaces arising in applications are nice; Theorem 2.1.22 (p. 54) concludes that (S,S) is nice. On the handbook route def:p15-measurable-real-coding (handbook/parts/p15/countable-product-measures.tex lines 174-180) only says that the source calls the class of its Theorem 2.1.22 nice and replaces the notion by the stronger Borel-image coding; the source definition, its exact relation to Borel real codings (every Borel real coding is a nice map; a nice map is a Borel real coding exactly when its image is Borel), the source's naming remark and applications claim, and the statement of Theorem 2.1.22 in the source's own terms are not supplied. Supply them on the route. (Unrouted text addressing this exists in packet w02ca-p15-002's handbook/parts/p15/probability-spaces-and-random-variables-w02c-p15-002.tex, def:p15-w02c-p15-002-nice and thm:p15-w02c-p15-002-nice-coding, lines 404-457; that packet lists this unit as read-only, owned by w02c-p15-004.)
components.note: Metric, completeness, separability, trace sigma-algebra, measurable isomorphism and Borel real coding are defined, but the source variant 'nice' (p. 53) is only named, not stated. No routed file defines it: the routed exchangeability chapter (handbook/parts/p15/exchangeability-and-predictive-induction-w02b-p15-022.tex lines 1009-1016 and 1067) uses 'nice space' without a definition.

Canonical digits with infinitely many zeros (source: 'taking the expansion with an infinite number of 0's') and theta(j,k) reproducing the source interleaving x^1_1 x^1_2 x^2_1 x^1_3 x^2_2 x^3_1 x^1_4 ... (p. 54); theta checked for the first ten positions.
Product metric rho(x,y) = sum |x_n - y_n|/2^n of the source special case, Borel image E_0, measurable inverse and boundary points, all proved.

Theorem 2.1.22's hypotheses (Borel S in a complete separable M, Borel subsets of S) and its proof steps (d = rho/(1+rho) of Exercise 2.1.3 proved directly, dense q_j in S, psi continuous and one-to-one, phi_o composed with psi) are supplied with the image and inverse made explicit; the conclusion is the stronger Borel real coding. The source's own wording of the conclusion depends on the definition missing under C009.

components.gap: ED26-P15-CH-countable-product-measures-C013 (partial): Durrett p. 53 states that Theorem 2.1.21 is not valid for arbitrary measurable spaces, attributes the first counterexample, on an infinite product of different spaces, to Andersen and Jessen (1948), referring to Halmos (1950) p. 214 and Neveu (1965) p. 84, refers to Wegner (1973) for a counterexample with all factor spaces equal, and asserts that for nice spaces the generalization of Kolmogorov's theorem is trivial. On the route thm:p15-coded-space-extension (handbook/parts/p15/countable-product-measures.tex lines 263-278; annex handbook/annex/p15/countable-product-measures.tex lines 456-512) proves the extension only for factors with Borel-image real codings, and its worked boundary says only that no extension assertion for arbitrary measurable spaces is inferred. The source's failure claim with all its attributions, and the source's nice-space generalization with the handbook's narrowing to Borel images stated against it, are not supplied. Supply them on the route. (Unrouted text in packet w02ca-p15-002's handbook/parts/p15/probability-spaces-and-random-variables-w02c-p15-002.tex, def:p15-w02c-p15-002-extension-limits and the paragraph after thm:p15-w02c-p15-002-nice-coding, lines 447-487, reports the failure claim and attributions.)
components.note: The Borel-coded extension is fully proved, but the source's p. 53 boundary and generalization claims are absent from the route.
Both worked boundaries (inconsistent marginals; null infinite intersection of positive cylinders) are stated with their reasons.
